newsitem.title: UK: Hushed BBC signifies end of Britain-historian.
newsitem.headline: Hushed BBC signifies end of Britain-historian.

text.p: BBC radio received a bizarre tribute on Thursday when a historian said the end of British civilisation in a nuclear war would be official when it ceased broadcasting.
Peter Hennessy said the final check by commanders of Britain's nuclear submarine fleet in the north Atlantic after a pre-emptive nuclear strike would be to turn on the BBC.

A deadly hush on the airwaves would be the signal for submarine commanders to open envelopes containing their final instructions for retaliation from the prime minister, Hennessy said in the preface to a new book "Muddling Through."
The professor of contemporary history at London's Queen Mary and Westfield College described the procedure as "a final if macabre tribute to a broadcasting service sans pareil."
"If the Trident commander could not pick up Today (a BBC news programme), that would be that," he told The Independent newspaper.
"He would then have to decide whether to launch the missiles, or go off to New Zealand. He would know there was no point in going back to base," Hennessy said.
